answer.decision: Choose logical replication with a brief write pause, validation, and traffic switch.
answer.action: Keep the source authoritative while logical replication catches up. During the approved window, pause and verify every write path, record the source replication position, wait until the target has applied through that position, and run CDC row-count, checksum, and critical transaction checks while writes remain paused. If validation succeeds with enough time remaining, atomically switch traffic to the target and resume writes; otherwise abort and resume writes on the unchanged source. Do not rely on switching back after target writes begin unless reverse replication or reconciliation has been separately designed and tested.
reasons: The rehearsed 42-second peak lag leaves substantial margin within the 10-minute write-unavailability cap.
The 30-minute big-bang freeze violates the approved limit, while the 96-minute export/import rehearsal is unsuitable for the cutover window.
Dual-write introduces significant omission and divergence risk because writes span 19 paths and three bypass the main repository layer.
Pausing writes, draining replication to a recorded source position, and validating before switching prevents acknowledged source writes from being silently omitted.
Keeping the source authoritative and unchanged until validation completes preserves the demonstrated rollback path.
assumptions: Production replication performance is close enough to staging performance to drain and validate within the maintenance cap.
All application, batch, administrative, and bypass write paths can be paused and their quiescence verified.
CDC checks and critical transaction tests are prepared, bounded, and capable of detecting unacceptable divergence.
The traffic switch is atomic or sufficiently coordinated to prevent writes from reaching both databases during transition.
risks: Production lag or validation could exceed rehearsal results, requiring an early abort to stay below 10 minutes.
An undiscovered or incompletely paused writer could cause divergence or lost writes.
Row counts and checksums may not detect every semantic or application-level defect.
The seven-minute rollback result applies only while the source remains authoritative; rollback after accepting target-only writes is not demonstrated.
With four engineers and no overnight vendor support, operational complexity and prolonged failures carry elevated response risk.

citations.claim: Peak synthetic-load staging replication lag was 42 seconds.
The application has 19 write paths across six modules, including three repository-layer bypasses.
Rollback completed in seven minutes when the source remained authoritative.
The largest production table is 1.8 TB, and full export/import took 96 minutes in rehearsal.
The approved maintenance window permits less than 10 minutes of write unavailability.
CDC monitoring can compare source and target row counts and checksums during cutover.
Logical replication with a brief write pause and validation is available; the big-bang alternative requires a 30-minute freeze.
